correctness.rationale: For all integers m>=4 and all positive real c,B, both Fourier-pair Rayleigh trace bounds apply to every independent nonnegative edge allocation. Equal-orbit allocations attain the minimum of these bounds because their Fourier spectrum has odd minimum D_m a+2b and even minimum A_m a. A two-line optimization determines all price regimes. Equality in the k=1 Rayleigh bound forces a genuine eigenvector equation; its imaginary parts force all cycle rates equal, and its real parts force all chord rates equal. Taylor expansions yield the claimed fourfold rate ratio and vanishing budget fraction. Standalone verify.py replayed VERIFY_OK 641; numerical checks only supplement proof.

value.rationale: Ring networks with diametral shortcuts are natural sparse diffusion designs. The exact all-optimizer theorem identifies a phase transition in deleting an entire edge class, the price at which a nontrivial interval of designs becomes equally best, and a quantitatively surprising fixed-price limit: a vanishing O(m^-2) spending fraction buys a fourfold leading spectral-gap improvement. This all-size structural result has meaningful network investment and preconditioning interpretations, and is not just an isolated numerical datum.
